Import an analysis dataset

Source: R/import_data.R
import_data.Rd

Read common tabular data formats through one consistent interface. Optional packages are required only for the formats that use them.

Usage

import_data(
  file,
  format = NULL,
  sheet = NULL,
  header = TRUE,
  sep = NULL,
  na = c("", "NA"),
  encoding = "UTF-8",
  name_repair = c("check_unique", "unique", "minimal"),
  ...
)

Arguments

file

Path to the data file.

format

Optional file format when it cannot be inferred from `file`. Supply an extension without the leading dot, such as `"csv"` or `"dta"`.

sheet

Excel sheet name or number. Used only for `.xls` and `.xlsx` files. The first sheet is used by default.

header

Logical; whether delimited text files contain column names.

sep

Optional delimiter for `.csv`, `.tsv`, and `.txt` files. Defaults to comma for CSV, tab for TSV, and whitespace for TXT.

na

Character vector of strings interpreted as missing values.

encoding

Character encoding used for delimited text files. With the default "UTF-8", a file that is not valid UTF-8 (typically a Latin-1 or Windows-1252 export) is read as Latin-1 and a message says so; set encoding explicitly to override.

name_repair

How to handle column names: `"check_unique"` preserves names and errors on blank or duplicated names; `"unique"` repairs them with [make.names()]; `"minimal"` preserves names without checking.

...

Additional arguments passed to the format-specific reader.

Value

A data frame. Tibbles and labelled columns returned by `readxl` or `haven` are retained.

Details

Supported extensions are CSV (`.csv`), tab-separated or text files (`.tsv`, `.txt`), Excel (`.xls`, `.xlsx`), R data (`.rds`), Stata (`.dta`), SPSS (`.sav`, `.zsav`, `.por`), and SAS (`.sas7bdat`, `.xpt`).

`readxl` is required for Excel files and `haven` is required for Stata, SPSS, and SAS files. RDS files must contain a data frame or tibble.

Examples

csv_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(
  data.frame(outcome = c(0, 1), age = c(45, 61)),
  csv_file,
  row.names = FALSE
)
imported <- import_data(csv_file)
names(imported)
#> [1] "outcome" "age"
